title: Remote Patient Monitoring Grant Program: Draft 1.0 Overview
summary: This grant program equips rural provider organizations with RPM hardware and software to shift care from reactive, high-cost episodes to proactive home-based monitoring. It targets chronic conditions like CHF, COPD, and Diabetes to reduce hospital readmissions.

children.text: The Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) Grant Program is designed to equip provider organizations—specifically home health agencies, primary care/specialty practices, and community paramedicine units—with the necessary hardware and software to monitor patients outside of clinical settings. By collecting real-time physiological data, clinicians can intervene earlier to prevent the deterioration of chronic conditions.

The program aims to distribute capital grants to rural providers to purchase compliant equipment. The strategic goal is to reduce expensive Emergency Department visits by managing high-risk patients in their homes before symptoms worsen.
Transforming Healthcare Delivery: From Reactive, High-Cost Episodes to Proactive, Home-Based Monitoring.

body.title: Eligible Device Capabilities

children.text: Successful applicants must ensure equipment supports 'connected diagnostic tools'. Given that 20% of rural Vermont lacks broadband, devices must offer cellular connectivity or store-and-forward capabilities. Additionally, all platforms must eventually integrate with the Vermont Health Information Exchange (VHIE) to ensure data does not remain siloed.
